product.name: [Product] Smart Pool Controller – Wi-Fi, app control, pH/chlorine dosing, pump & heater control

product.intendedPurpose: Automated control of private swimming pool water treatment (pH / chlorine dosing), filtration pump and heater, with monitoring and control via mobile app and cloud.
product.foreseeableUse: Installed by consumers without professional help; setup left half-finished; weak or reused account passwords; shared household logins; insecure home Wi-Fi with other compromised IoT devices; resale with account still bound; use after end of support; pool service companies managing many customers' devices.
product.users: Owner (admin) · household members (shared access) · pool service technician (delegated access) · voice assistant / smart-home integration
product.environment: Private homes, outdoor technical room; consumer Wi-Fi router without IT management; children and swimmers present; manufacturer cloud in EU region.
product.essentialFunctions: Safe dosing limits (never exceed max dose); filtration; frost protection; local operation without cloud.
product.safetyFunctions: Chemical dosing (chlorine, acid), heater control. Limits enforced in firmware/hardware, not in app or cloud.
product.rdps: User account & device cloud, app backend, push-notification service, OTA service
product.outOfScope: Consumer's router and phone OS; third-party voice-assistant clouds (integration interface IS in scope)
product.personalData: Account data, location (pool address / weather), usage patterns revealing presence, push tokens

risks.scenario: Account takeover via credential stuffing; attacker changes dosing setpoints or disables filtration.
risks.consequence: Pool water unsafe; equipment damage; user locked out
risks.controls: Breached-password check and minimum password policy; rate limiting and lockout; optional MFA (offered prominently); new-login notifications; safety limits enforced in firmware regardless of cloud command.

risks.scenario: Manipulated command or corrupted sensor value causes chemical overdose (chlorine / acid).
risks.vector: Any control path to dosing pumps
risks.consequence: Health hazard to swimmers (skin, eyes, lungs)
risks.controls: Max dose per hour and per day enforced in firmware/hardware, not changeable remotely; flow-switch interlock (no dosing without circulation); plausibility checks on pH/ORP readings; range-validated commands; dosing events logged and notified.
risks.evidence: Safety test report; fault-injection test TC-DOSE-01..04

risks.scenario: Unauthenticated local API lets any device on the home LAN (e.g. a compromised camera) control the pool.
risks.controls: Local API disabled by default; when enabled, requires token bound to owner account; TLS; no UPnP / port forwarding.
risks.evidence: Port scan of default config; API auth test

risks.scenario: Open or weakly protected provisioning (SoftAP / BLE) lets a nearby attacker capture the home Wi-Fi password or claim the device.
risks.controls: Per-device setup code from label / QR; encrypted provisioning channel; setup mode times out and requires physical button to re-enter; device claiming bound to first authenticated owner.

risks.scenario: Device recruited into a botnet through an outdated third-party component and used to attack others.
risks.consequence: Harm to third parties; device unstable
risks.controls: Minimal exposed services; SBOM per release; vulnerability monitoring with patch SLA; release gate: no known exploitable vulnerabilities; outbound traffic limits.

risks.scenario: Users never install updates, so fixed vulnerabilities stay exploitable in the field.
risks.consequence: Known exploitable vulnerabilities in the field
risks.controls: Automatic security updates on by default; user notified, can postpone; clear opt-out; security fixes delivered separately from feature updates; update status visible in app.
risks.evidence: Update telemetry: % fleet on latest FW

risks.scenario: After resale, previous owner keeps app access or personal data remains on device / in cloud.
risks.consequence: Privacy breach; previous owner controls new owner's pool
risks.controls: Factory reset on device removes all user data and unbinds account; owner transfer flow in app; cloud data deletion on unbind; new owner sees list of users with access.

risks.scenario: Cloud breach exposes usage patterns showing when households are absent (vacation mode, heating off).
risks.controls: Data minimisation (no exact location stored, only weather region); encryption at rest; retention limits; access logging; vacation mode not exposed in third-party integrations.

risks.scenario: Cloud outage or end of cloud service leaves the pool without control or makes the device unusable.
risks.controls: Controller runs autonomously on last valid schedule and safety limits; local control via button / display; documented end-of-support behaviour shown to users.

risks.scenario: Debug port used to extract a key or credential shared across all devices, enabling fleet-wide impersonation.
risks.vector: UART / JTAG on a purchased unit
risks.controls: Unique per-device keys in secure element; debug interfaces locked / disabled in production; flash encryption; no hard-coded credentials.

risks.scenario: Voice-assistant / smart-home integration token abused to control pool functions.
risks.controls: Scoped OAuth tokens; safety-relevant functions (dosing) not exposed to integrations; token revocation in app; integration disabled by default.

P1-2b.implementation: Local API, integrations and debug off by default; unique per-device setup code; factory reset button.
